entry.title: ML 02 Gradient Descent
entry.content:
1 update w, b

  • $$ \left\{ \begin{aligned} w &= w - \alpha \frac{\partial}{\partial w} J(w,b) \\ b &= b - \alpha \frac{\partial}{\partial b} J(w,b) \end{aligned} \right. $$ Simultaneously update w and b, like that: $$ \begin{aligned} tmp\_w &= w - \alpha \frac{\partial}{\partial w} J(w,b) \\ tmp\_b &= b - \alpha \frac{\partial}{\partial b} J(w,b) \\ w &= tmp\_w \\ b &= tmp\_b \end{aligned} $$
  • α is the learning rate,controls the step length when updating w and b.
    • if α is too small, thegradient descent will work at a very ==slow speed== and will take a longtime
    • if α is too large, thegradient descent may overshoot and never reach minimum, it fail toconverge, ==may even diverge==
  • why the gradient descent change w to get J(w) closer to the minimum(one parameter condition, without b)
  • if the J(w) has already reach the ==local== minimum, then thefurther gradient descent will do absolutely nothing
  • as J(w) approachs the minimum, the derivative gets closer to zero,if the α is fixed, updatesteps become smaller

2 calculate:

  • when you use a suqared error cost function with linear regression,the cost function only have one minimum, the global minimum. and thecost function is a convex function, like this one:
  • it will always coverge to the minimum if you choose a appropriatelearning rate.

3 “Batch” gradient descent

  • meaning: each step of gradient descent uses ==all the trainingexamples==.

4 meanings

  • Monitoring J
    • when the decreasing speed down to some special number
    • or set a Epochs, a number of iterations
  • Monitoring Gradients
    • the $\left| \frac{\partial J}{\partial w}\right|$ and $\left| \frac{\partialJ}{\partial b} \right|$ will become smaller after everyiterations, so we can set very small limits:$$\left| \frac{\partial J}{\partial w} \right| <\epsilon \quad \text{and} \quad \left| \frac{\partial J}{\partial b}\right| < \epsilon$$ when the two derivatives reach the limitssimultaneously, the function converges.
  • Monitoring Δw andΔb
    • the change in parameter Δw is proportional to thegradient we can see in the gradient descent, so when the gradient closeto 0, the change of w and b will become smaller. so we set a threshold,when the changes get smaller than the threshold, the functionconverges.

entry.title: Machine Learning 01
entry.content:
Machine Learning algorithms

  • supervised learnning, used most
  • unsupervised learning
  • recommender systems
  • reinforcement learing

notation

  • x = ‘input’ variable / feature
  • y = ‘output’ variable / ‘target’ variable
  • ŷ = predicted value
  • m = number of traing example
  • (x, y) = single traing example
  • (xi, yi) = ithtraining example (1st, 2nd, 3rd, ...)

supervised learning

  • give the system a pair of X label and Y label, after learning,the system will learn how to give a resonably accurate prediction ofthe output. Learning input-output or x-to-y mappings.

  • Regression algorithm

    • Predict a number from infinitely many possible numbers.
    • Linear Regression model
      • cost function
        • linear function, e.g. fw, b(x) = wx + b
        • w,b is parameters/coefficients/weights
        • ŷ(i) = f(x(i))
        • total squared error: measures how far off the prediction is from thetarget: $$\sum\limits_{i=1}^{m} (\hat{y}^{(i)} - y^{(i)} )^2$$
        • cost function / squared error cost function: $$J(w, b) = \frac{1}{2m} \sum\limits_{i=1}^{m} (\hat{y}^{(i)} - y^{(i)} )^2$$ equals to $$J(w, b) = \frac{1}{2m} \sum\limits_{i=1}^{m} (f_{w,b}(x^{(i)}) - y^{(i)} )^2$$
        • goal: find $$\min\limits_{w,b} J(w,b)$$
      • ML 02 Gradient Descent #

  • Classification algorithm

    • classification predicts a small. finite, limited set of possibleoutput catagories.
    • classification model predicts categories or discrete categories

unsupervised learning

  • find some structure or some pattern, not asked to give some quoteright answer

  • clustering algorithm

    • takes data without labels and tries to automatically group them intoclusters.
    • group similar data together

  • anomaly detection

    • find unusual data points

  • dimensionality reduction

    • compress data , with losing as little information as possible
